A1.cefrDesc: Ability to form basic daily expressions and simple sentences for concrete needs.
A1.objective: Introducing yourself and your profession, describing routines, ordering in a café, and asking about time/price.
A1.topics.0.title: Subject Pronouns & Verb To Be (Am / Is / Are)
A1.topics.0.description: Expresses identity, profession, age, origin, and current states.
A1.topics.1.title: Articles (A, An, The) & Demonstratives (This, That, These, Those)
A1.topics.1.description: Indicates objects and defines definite/indefinite nouns.
A1.topics.2.title: Possessive Adjectives & Possessive 's
A1.topics.2.description: Indicates possession, ownership, and family/work relationships.
A1.topics.3.title: Present Simple Tense (Geniş Zaman)
A1.topics.3.description: Describes daily routines, habits, and unchanging facts.
A1.topics.3.examples.0.tr: I write clean code every day.
A1.topics.3.examples.1.tr: He works at a tech startup.
A1.topics.4.title: Adverbs of Frequency (Always, Usually, Often, Sometimes, Never)
A1.topics.4.description: Expresses how often actions are done.
A1.topics.4.examples.0.tr: I always test my code before pushing.
A1.topics.4.examples.1.tr: She is never late for meetings.
A1.topics.5.title: Present Continuous Tense (Şimdiki Zaman)
A1.topics.5.description: Describes actions happening right now and temporary states.
A1.topics.5.examples.0.tr: We are developing a new mobile application.
A1.topics.5.examples.1.tr: He is debugging the authentication issue.
A1.topics.6.title: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns & Quantifiers (Some, Any, Much, Many)
A1.topics.6.description: Indicates quantity, places orders, and queries existence.
A1.topics.6.examples.0.tr: Do you have any questions about the database?
A1.topics.6.examples.1.tr: There is some information in the documentation.
A1.topics.7.title: There is / There are & Prepositions of Place
A1.topics.7.description: Describes the physical location of objects and places.
A1.topics.7.examples.0.tr: There is an error on line 42.
A1.topics.7.examples.1.tr: There are three servers in the rack.
A1.topics.8.title: Modal Verb: Can / Can't (Ability, Permission & Requests)
A1.topics.8.description: Abilities, permissions, and polite requests in a café/office.
A1.topics.8.examples.0.tr: She can build responsive web layouts.
A1.topics.8.examples.1.tr: Can we access the staging server?
A1.topics.9.title: Past Simple: Verb To Be (Was / Were)
A1.topics.9.description: Describes past states, locations, and descriptions of places.
A1.topics.9.examples.1.tr: We were in the lab all morning.
A1.topics.10.title: Past Simple Tense (Regular & Irregular Verbs, Did)
A1.topics.10.description: Describes completed actions and memories from the past.
A1.topics.10.examples.0.tr: I fixed the bug and deployed the update.
A1.topics.10.examples.1.tr: Did you receive my email this morning?
A1.topics.11.title: Future Tense: Will vs. Be Going To
A1.topics.11.description: Future plans, instant decisions, and predictions.
A1.topics.11.examples.0.tr: I am going to launch the beta version next month.
A1.topics.11.examples.1.tr: Wait, I will help you with this script.
A1.units.0.title: Meeting and Identity
A1.units.1.title: Daily Routines
A1.units.2.title: The World Around You
A1.units.3.title: Past and Future
A1.bossChallenge.title: A1 ➔ A2 Level Up Conversation
A1.bossChallenge.description: A free assessment conversation including meeting Mivo, daily routines, and simple ordering sentences.

A2.cefrDesc: Fluent communication about personal and family information, shopping, travel, and past experiences.
A2.objective: Airport check-in, hotel booking, giving directions, detailed storytelling of past memories, and making comparisons.
A2.topics.0.title: Comparatives & Superlatives (-er/more than & the -est/the most)
A2.topics.0.description: Comparing two or more objects, products, or situations.
A2.topics.0.examples.0.tr: PostgreSQL is more powerful than SQLite for large datasets.
A2.topics.0.examples.1.tr: This is the easiest framework to learn.
A2.topics.1.title: Past Continuous Tense
A2.topics.1.description: Actions that were ongoing at a specific moment in the past.
A2.topics.1.examples.0.tr: I was writing the backend logic at 9 PM yesterday.
A2.topics.1.examples.1.tr: They were testing the payment system all afternoon.
A2.topics.2.title: Past Simple vs. Past Continuous with When & While
A2.topics.2.description: 'While' introduces the longer action in the background, 'When' introduces the shorter action.
A2.topics.2.examples.0.tr: While I was deploying the app, the connection dropped.
A2.topics.2.examples.1.tr: We were testing the API when the server crashed.
A2.topics.3.title: Modals: Should, Must, Have To, Could, May, Might
A2.topics.3.description: 'Should' indicates advice, 'Must/Have to' indicates obligation, 'Could/May/Might' indicates possibility.
A2.topics.3.examples.0.tr: You should refactor this function to improve performance.
A2.topics.3.examples.1.tr: We have to deliver the milestone by Friday.
A2.topics.4.title: Quantifiers & Indefinite Pronouns (A few, A little, Too, Enough, Someone)
A2.topics.4.description: 'A few' is for countable, 'A little' is for uncountable; 'Too' indicates excess, 'Enough' indicates sufficiency.
A2.topics.4.examples.0.tr: We have a few minor issues to solve.
A2.topics.4.examples.1.tr: The query is fast enough for production.
A2.topics.5.title: Gerunds vs. Infinitives (Like doing vs. Want to do)
A2.topics.5.description: Some verbs take -ing (gerund), others take to + verb (infinitive).
A2.topics.5.examples.0.tr: I enjoy developing mobile interfaces with Compose.
A2.topics.5.examples.1.tr: We decided to migrate our database.
A2.topics.6.title: Conditionals: Zero & First Conditional
A2.topics.6.description: Type 0 is for general truths/scientific facts, Type 1 is used for real future possibilities.
A2.topics.6.examples.0.tr: If you input invalid credentials, the system throws an error.
A2.topics.6.examples.1.tr: If we optimize the images, the page will load much faster.
A2.topics.7.title: Present Perfect Tense (have/has + V3)
A2.topics.7.description: Connects the past to the present; used for unspecified life experiences (just, already, yet, ever, never).
A2.topics.7.examples.0.tr: I have already configured the SSL certificate.
A2.topics.7.examples.1.tr: Have you ever used Docker in production?
A2.topics.8.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
A2.topics.8.description: Use Past Simple for definite time, Present Perfect for experience/current effect.
A2.topics.8.examples.0.tr: I built the prototype last month (Past Simple).
A2.topics.8.examples.1.tr: I have built three full-stack apps so far (Present Perfect).
A2.topics.9.title: Prepositions of Movement & Linking Words
A2.topics.9.description: Connect ideas logically in terms of cause, effect, and contrast.
A2.topics.9.examples.0.tr: Although the library is new, it has great documentation.
A2.topics.9.examples.1.tr: The API key was invalid, so the request failed.
A2.units.0.title: Comparison and Past Tense
A2.units.1.title: Rules and Probabilities
A2.units.2.title: Conditions, Experience, and Connectors
A2.bossChallenge.title: A2 ➔ B1 Level Up Conversation
A2.bossChallenge.description: A free assessment conversation covering travel, problem-solving, and sharing past experiences with Mivo.

B1.cefrDesc: Independently express opinions and solve problems in work, school, and travel situations.
B1.objective: Defend yourself in job interviews, visa interviews, technical discussions, and justify opinions.
B1.topics.0.title: Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been + V-ing)
B1.topics.0.description: Emphasizes the duration and continuity of an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
B1.topics.0.examples.0.tr: I have been working on this machine learning model for three hours.
B1.topics.0.examples.1.tr: The server has been running without errors since Monday.
B1.topics.1.title: Past Perfect Simple (had + V3)
B1.topics.1.description: Indicates what happened before two events in the past, usually used with 'before/after/by the time'.
B1.topics.1.examples.0.tr: By the time we deployed the hotfix, the users had already reported the issue.
B1.topics.1.examples.1.tr: I had saved my changes before the power outage occurred.
B1.topics.2.title: Second Conditional (Unreal Present / Hypotheses)
B1.topics.2.description: Used for imaginary, unreal, or impossible situations related to the present.
B1.topics.2.examples.0.tr: If I had more computing power, I would train a larger neural network.
B1.topics.2.examples.1.tr: If we used automated tests, we would save hours of manual QA.
B1.topics.3.title: Defining & Non-Defining Relative Clauses (who, which, that, where, whose)
B1.topics.3.description: Defining clauses carry essential identity without commas, non-defining ones add extra information with commas.
B1.topics.3.examples.0.tr: The engineer who designed this microservice is lead architect.
B1.topics.3.examples.1.tr: FastAPI, which is built on Starlette, provides automatic API docs.
B1.topics.4.title: Passive Voice (Present Simple, Past Simple, Future, Modals)
B1.topics.4.description: Focus shifts from the doer to the receiver or the action itself.
B1.topics.4.examples.0.tr: User passwords are encrypted before being stored in the database.
B1.topics.4.examples.1.tr: The pull request was reviewed and approved by the team lead.
B1.topics.5.title: Modals of Deduction & Speculation (Must be, Can't be, Might be)
B1.topics.5.description: 'Must be' indicates strong positive inference, 'Can't be' indicates strong negative inference, 'Might/Could be' indicates possibility.
B1.topics.5.examples.0.tr: The port is already in use; another process must be running on port 8080.
B1.topics.5.examples.1.tr: This cannot be a database issue because the connection pool is healthy.
B1.topics.6.title: Used to & Would for Past Habits
B1.topics.6.description: 'Used to' describes both past states and actions, 'Would' describes only repeated past actions.
B1.topics.6.examples.0.tr: We used to maintain monolithic architectures before migrating to containers.
B1.topics.6.examples.1.tr: Every Friday, we would review our open pull requests together.
B1.topics.7.title: Reported Speech (Statements & Questions)
B1.topics.7.description: If the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, asked), the tenses shift back one step.
B1.topics.7.examples.0.tr: The client said that the endpoint was returning a 500 error.
B1.topics.7.examples.1.tr: She asked me whether the documentation was up to date.
B1.topics.8.title: Complex Gerunds & Infinitives (remember to do vs. remember doing)
B1.topics.8.description: 'Remember to do' expresses a future task, 'Remember doing' refers to a past memory.
B1.topics.8.examples.0.tr: Remember to sanitize user input before running SQL queries.
B1.topics.8.examples.1.tr: I remember compiling the binary without any compiler warnings.
B1.topics.9.title: Phrasal Verbs (Separable vs. Inseparable)
B1.topics.9.description: Phrasal verbs that can be separated must be separated when used with pronouns (turn it off, set it up).
B1.topics.9.examples.0.tr: Let's set up the staging environment on a dedicated virtual machine.
B1.topics.9.examples.1.tr: You should turn it on after verifying the network configuration.
B1.units.0.title: Continuity and Conditions
B1.units.1.title: Sentence Structures and Inference
B1.units.2.title: Reported Speech and Phrasal Verbs
B1.bossChallenge.title: B1 ➔ B2 Level Up Conversation
B1.bossChallenge.description: A free assessment conversation involving technical discussion, justification, and argument defense with Mivo.

B2.cefrDesc: Understanding main ideas of complex texts, fluent and instant reasoning in technical discussions.
B2.objective: Managing B2B sales meetings, architectural design presentations, diplomatic negotiations, and spontaneous persuasion.
B2.topics.0.title: Third & Mixed Conditionals (Past Regrets & Hybrid Timelines)
B2.topics.0.description: Type 3 refers to impossible past conditions/regrets, Mixed Conditionals link a past action to a present result.
B2.topics.0.examples.0.tr: If we had validated the schema before migration, the service wouldn't have failed.
B2.topics.0.examples.1.tr: If I had taken the cloud certification last year, I would lead the DevOps team today.
B2.topics.1.title: Future Continuous & Future Perfect (will be doing / will have done)
B2.topics.1.description: Future Continuous describes an action that will be ongoing in the future, Future Perfect describes an action that will have been completed by a point in the future.
B2.topics.1.examples.0.tr: This time next week, we will be presenting our system at the tech summit.
B2.topics.1.examples.1.tr: By December, our team will have shipped the entire enterprise platform.
B2.topics.2.title: Past Modals of Deduction & Regret (must have, can’t have, should have, could have)
B2.topics.2.description: 'Must have been' indicates a strong inference about the past, 'Should have done' indicates an unfulfilled past task/regret.
B2.topics.2.examples.0.tr: The hacker must have exploited an unpatched zero-day vulnerability.
B2.topics.2.examples.1.tr: We should have implemented rate limiting to prevent DDoS attacks.
B2.topics.3.title: Inversion with Negative Adverbials (Seldom, Rarely, Hardly, Not only... but also)
B2.topics.3.description: Creates stylistic/emphatic effect in formal writing and technical presentations.
B2.topics.3.examples.0.tr: Rarely have we encountered such a catastrophic memory corruption.
B2.topics.3.examples.1.tr: Not only does this framework support SSR, but it also optimizes hydration.
B2.topics.4.title: Participle Clauses (-ing and -ed clauses)
B2.topics.4.description: Creates concise, professional academic/technical prose by shortening long subordinate clauses.
B2.topics.4.examples.0.tr: Having compiled the source code, the CI pipeline triggered automated integration tests.
B2.topics.4.examples.1.tr: Stored in encrypted volumes, the database backups remain completely safe.
B2.topics.5.title: Causative Verbs (Have/Get something done, Make, Let)
B2.topics.5.description: Indicates the meaning of arranging or delegating for an action to be done by another party.
B2.topics.5.examples.0.tr: We need to have our infrastructure audited by third-party security researchers.
B2.topics.5.examples.1.tr: The new update lets users customize their dashboard layout.
B2.topics.6.title: Advanced Passive: Reporting Verbs & Impersonal Passive
B2.topics.6.description: It expresses a common view in technical reports and formal discourse in a neutral way.
B2.topics.6.examples.0.tr: Quantum computing is estimated to revolutionize cryptographic protocols.
B2.topics.6.examples.1.tr: It is widely acknowledged that distributed systems introduce network latency.
B2.topics.7.title: Subjunctive Mood in Formal English
B2.topics.7.description: The verb in the 'that' clause remains in the base form, regardless of the subject's person/tense.
B2.topics.7.examples.0.tr: We strongly recommend that the administrator revoke all compromised tokens immediately.
B2.topics.7.examples.1.tr: It is imperative that every database transaction be atomic.
B2.units.0.title: Assumptions and Future
B2.units.1.title: Advanced Sentence Structures
B2.bossChallenge.title: B2 ➔ C1 Level Up Conversation
B2.bossChallenge.description: A free assessment conversation involving a corporate presentation with Mivo and handling challenging objections.

C1.cefrDesc: Understanding challenging and lengthy texts, using the language flexibly for social, academic, and professional purposes.
C1.objective: High-level management presentations, international negotiations, subtle rhetoric, and cultural nuances.
C1.topics.0.title: Cleft Sentences for Focus & Emphasis (It-clefts, Wh-clefts)
C1.topics.0.description: It emphasizes a specific subject, predicate, or object by splitting a simple sentence in two.
C1.topics.0.examples.0.tr: It was the race condition in the thread pool that corrupted our state.
C1.topics.0.examples.1.tr: What we fundamentally aim to achieve is sub-millisecond query latency.
C1.topics.1.title: Advanced Inversion in Conditional Clauses (Without 'If')
C1.topics.1.description: 'If' is removed and the auxiliary verb is placed at the front — used in highly formal academic/legal language.
C1.topics.1.examples.0.tr: Had we executed full regression suites, this regression would never have reached staging.
C1.topics.1.examples.1.tr: Should the primary cluster experience failover, the replica assumes immediate master status.
C1.topics.2.title: Absolute Participle Clauses & Complex Ellipsis
C1.topics.2.description: It is a structure that provides a dense academic context with an independent subject of the participle.
C1.topics.2.examples.0.tr: All dependencies having been validated, the runtime initialized the microkernel safely.
C1.topics.2.examples.1.tr: Some processes consume GPU memory, others CPU cache.
C1.topics.3.title: Nominalization & Formal Academic Discourse Markers
C1.topics.3.description: It creates authoritative, dense, impersonal scientific and engineering prose.
C1.topics.3.examples.0.tr: The rapid proliferation of edge nodes necessitates rigorous telemetry aggregation.
C1.topics.3.examples.1.tr: Notwithstanding the preliminary benchmarks, empirical data substantiates our hypothesis.
C1.units.0.title: Emphasis Structures
C1.units.1.title: Academic Discourse
C1.bossChallenge.title: C1 ➔ C2 Mastery Conversation
C1.bossChallenge.description: A free assessment conversation themed around international crisis management and diplomatic consensus with Mivo.

C2.cefrDesc: Effortlessly understanding everything heard and read, expressing spontaneously, fluently, and accurately at a native level.
C2.objective: Native-level rhetoric, diplomatic negotiation, philosophical argument development, and absolute language mastery.
C2.topics.0.title: Stylistic & Rhetorical Inversion and Fronting
C2.topics.0.description: Creates dramatic rhetorical tempo and fluid thematic coherence in high-level literature and executive discourse.
C2.topics.0.examples.0.tr: Embedded within the cryptographic envelope lies the immutable ledger of transactions.
C2.topics.0.examples.1.tr: Gone are the days when monolithic single-threaded engines could suffice.
C2.topics.1.title: Pragmatic Subtlety, Nuance & Complex Sentence Restructuring
C2.topics.1.description: Enables fine-tuning of tone, intellectual distance, irony, and diplomatic sensitivity.
C2.topics.1.examples.0.tr: Far be it from me to cast aspersions on the architectural design, yet the algorithmic overhead remains untenable.
C2.topics.1.examples.1.tr: Be that as it may, the empirical consensus favors asynchronous reconciliation.
C2.units.0.title: Mastery Level Rhetoric
C2.bossChallenge.title: C2 Language Mastery Conversation 👑
C2.bossChallenge.description: A free-topic conversation with Mivo, assessing top-level fluency and vocabulary richness.
